overall.summary: The age part's plain hypothesis swaps Ireland and Thailand, and the self-employment technical hypothesis states 12.4% of rows instead of 7.8%; coverage, preservation, closed forms, all 200 claims and every ablation otherwise reproduce, with some off-support category statements weakened.

findings.statement: lowest at about 47 years and higher either side, except for people born in Ireland, for whom it rises with age; being born in Thailand lowers it
findings.check: probe age 22..70 for the United States, Ireland and Thailand (typical person otherwise)
findings.evidence: Ireland and Thailand are swapped. Ireland keeps the V shape, shifted down: 61.1% at 22, 20.5% at 46 (lowest), 34.8% at 70; age-part contribution is the US value minus 1.57 at every age. Thailand is the group whose chance rises with age: 66.0% at 22, 76.1% at 38, 80.2% at 46, 89.5% at 70. Being Thai lowers the chance only for young people (66.0% vs 84.1% at 22, 71.3% vs 74.3% at 30); from about 32 years on it raises it (76.1% vs 61.4% at 38, 80.2% vs 46.5% at 46, 89.5% vs 64.2% at 70). The part's own evidence sentences (C139 Thailand rises 66%->85%; C136 Ireland lowers 63%->26%) say the opposite of this hypothesis.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-785c68 --sweep age=22:70:7 --sweep native-country=39,21,37

findings.statement: Adds +0.646 to the logit of P(<=50K) for that group (12.4% of rows), 0 otherwise
findings.evidence: n = 3034 of 39073 = 7.8% of training rows, not 12.4%. The part is active for exactly those 3034 (0% elsewhere), mean contribution +0.6456. The part's own evidence record says 7.8%. The +0.646, 8292 = 1.822 and 5559 = 1.49 values reproduce.

findings.evidence: The model's minimum is at about 46.1 years (score -0.146 at 46.1; -0.139 at 46, -0.121 at 47), matching the technical hypothesis (vertex 46). findings.statement: A highest education of 7th-8th grade lowers it to about 35%, 9th grade to about 44% and 10th grade to about 49% (same sentence in drafted.blocks[1][3])
findings.check: probe education x education-num; subgroup education == '5' and education-num != 4
findings.evidence: The numbers reproduce but only for an impossible person: the category is changed while education level stays at 10. All 739 training 7th-8th graders have education level 4 (0 rows otherwise). With matching levels the model does the opposite: high-school graduate (level 9) 71.5%, 7th-8th grade (level 4) 84.6%, 9th grade (5) 84.4%, 10th grade (6) 82.0%. The sentence is extrapolation outside the data and misleads about what the model does for real people. The worth_checking flag [4] correctly flags it.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-785c68 --sweep education=11,5,6,0 --sweep education-num=9,4,5,6 --no-parts
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-785c68 --where "education == '5' and `education-num` != 4"
